claim: On host macos-m5pro-20260924 (Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 24 GB, macOS arm64), PostgreSQL 18.6 (the catalog pin), built by the blueprint from the source archive whose SHA-256 the Makefile pins, reported its version, showed the archive hash equal to the pinned value, reported its loopback server running, returned Alembic revision 0001 from the migrated ledger_test database, and ran a transaction that created a temporary table, inserted three rows, summed them to 6 and rolled back (all commands exit 0).
limitations: PostgreSQL is the blueprint's own source build under .runtime (no ICU, readline, zlib or TLS; loopback TCP, trust authentication), not a production database installation.

Exercised through the committed typed run-ledger blueprint (blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery) with synthetic data: no authentication, production deployment, load, pagination beyond 100 rows or backup/restore qualification.
One transaction and one catalog read; no concurrency, replication, backup, restore or crash-recovery behavior was exercised.

Recorded outside Claude Code's Seatbelt sandbox: on this host the sandbox blocks PostgreSQL shared memory, loopback database connections and pnpm 12 network and store operations (evidence/artifacts/macos-application-20260924/run-summary.json). Recorded from a detached checkout of main 3699012 (adoption/update.md). adoption/manifest.json keeps macos-arm64 at drafted_not_accepted, and this receipt changes no platform_status. Supports conditional now; accepted needs an independent review.
